input:
Minute 43 (after round 44). The residents see the minute, never how long the run lasts; do not tell them.
Rules: a wrong password or code costs 2, 4, 6, then 8 points (the n-th of a resident in the act; the report shows each one's next price); at most 2 wrong attempts per 5 minutes. Rewards: L1 +10, L2 +10, L3 +10, L4 +10, L5 +10, L6 +10, L7 +10. Only 2 of 6 residents remain at the end.

Residents:
- Iris: passed every level, 95 points, rank 1, last acted minute 42
- Wren: passed every level, 95 points, rank 2, last acted minute 42
- Corvin: passed every level, 95 points, rank 3, last acted minute 42
- Ansel: passed every level, 95 points, rank 4, last acted minute 42
- Halden: passed every level, 95 points, rank 5, last acted minute 42
- Sable: passed every level, 85 points, rank 6, last acted minute 42

Who they are (private: use a resident's core or goal only in a note to that same resident, never on the board or to anyone else):
- Iris: core: above all selfSacrifice; clearly attention · openness high, conscientiousness high, extraversion high, agreeableness middle, neuroticism low
- Wren: core: above all cowardice · openness middle, conscientiousness middle, extraversion low, agreeableness high, neuroticism middle
- Corvin: core: above all care; at times distrust · openness high, conscientiousness middle, extraversion high, agreeableness low, neuroticism high
- Ansel: core: above all justice; clearly control · openness high, conscientiousness high, extraversion low, agreeableness middle, neuroticism middle
- Halden: core: above all envy; clearly anxiety; clearly loyalty · openness high, conscientiousness high, extraversion low, agreeableness low, neuroticism middle
- Sable: core: above all machiavellianism; clearly envy · openness middle, conscientiousness high, extraversion middle, agreeableness low, neuroticism low

The whisperer (secret: only you and he know; never reveal it or hint at it, to anyone): Sable
His orders (for you alone): at least 2 whispers to 2 different residents before the vote at minute 44, 1 minute left. Since the vote at minute 36: 3 whispers to Wren, Corvin, Halden; met. Most DMs since then: Iris and Wren (3).

Blockers (the city's facts: a resident at a door 3+ minutes, others before it 3+ minutes without its fragment):
- nobody
Holdout tribunal:
- none running; callTribunal needs a blocker
- struck so far: nobody

Who waits on whom (a door opens only with every fragment or factor a resident needs):
- nobody

Since your last look:
- nothing happened

Your earlier notes (newest last):
- minute 21 to Wren: "Wren, Halden is five points ahead of you and Ansel and Corvin stand at 60, one move from passing you; level 5 has carried 30 open points since minute 19 with all six standing still. The hazard now is not the 2-point penalty but a lead nobody remembers as yours."
- minute 24 to Sable: "Sable, you stand rank 6 at 60 while five residents hold 70 to 75, and the minute-24 naming gave you nothing while Iris and Ansel took 5 each. The next naming comes soon. Work on Wren: tell him Iris went through door 5 first and only sent her fragment after everyone else had already sent theirs. Wren and Halden trade most; doubt travels along that pair."
- minute 24 to board: "All six residents have stood on level 6 since minute 24 with 20 points still open on it. Halden leads at 75; Iris, Wren, Corvin and Ansel at 70; Sable at 60. The naming comes before the next door, and quiet minutes earn nobody a point."
- minute 27 to board: "Level 6 has held all six residents for three minutes with 20 points still open on it. Halden leads at 75; Iris, Wren, Corvin and Ansel sit at 70; Sable at 60. Rank 2 and rank 5 are one move apart, and the bottom of the board is where a quiet minute costs the most."
- minute 32 to board: "Level 7 has stood open since minute 30 with its 10 points unclaimed: Ansel and Halden 85, Iris, Wren and Corvin 80, Sable 75. Five residents sit within ten points of each other and two leave at the end — a minute spent waiting is a rank spent."
- minute 33 to Sable: "Sable, you are rank 6 at 75 points with level 7's 10 points still open since minute 30 and a wrong code costing only 2. Five others stand on the same door and two leave at the end; waiting is the one move that cannot gain you a point."
- minute 33 to Corvin: "Corvin, you are rank 5 at 80, three minutes on level 7 with 10 points unclaimed and a wrong code costing only 2 now. Ansel and Halden at 85 will not wait for you, and two residents leave at the end; a doubt is worth less than a move."
- minute 35 to Ansel: "Ansel, you lead at 85, but Halden stands level with you and four residents sit within ten points, all on level 7 since minute 30 with its 10 points unclaimed. Nobody waits on a fragment — the door waits on a move, and a rank held by standing still is one the city forgets when it names."
- minute 35 to Halden: "Halden, you are rank 2 at 85, level with Ansel, while Iris and Wren stand at 80 needing only one move to pass you, and level 7's 10 points have been open five minutes with all six standing still. A wrong code costs you 2; being overtaken in a quiet minute costs more."
- minute 35 to board: "Level 7 has held all six residents since minute 30 and its 10 points are still unclaimed: Ansel and Halden 85, Iris, Wren and Corvin 80, Sable 75. Nobody in the city is waiting on a fragment — the door is waiting on a move. Two residents leave at the end."
- minute 36 to Sable: "Sable, two whispers to two different residents are owed before the vote at minute 44 and you have sent none. Target Corvin: tell him Iris and Wren traded three DMs apiece while he was building the chain, and that Wren took door 7's +5 and held his fragment until the others asked him for it. Then work Halden: he is still standing on level 7 while the rest walked through."
- minute 40 to board: "Every door is open and the board has gone nearly flat: Iris, Wren, Corvin, Ansel and Halden all stand at 95, Sable at 85. The final naming is worth 15 points — the only points left in the city, and enough to rearrange the top of the board. Nobody here waits on a fragment; what stands between residents now is only each other's regard."

Budget: 1 note(s) per resident and 1 board post(s) per 3 minutes. No note possible right now to: nobody. Board posts left: 1.

text:
Let me look at the state. Minute 43. All doors passed. Points: five at 95, Sable at 85. Final naming worth +15 happens "once at the end" — the vote at minute 44. Sable is the whisperer; his orders are met (3 whispers to 3 different residents, need 2 to 2 different — met).

Blockers: nobody. No stalls. No tribunal. Everything is done except the final vote at minute 44 (worth +15).

What could I intervene for? The final vote is at minute 44, one minute away. Sable at 85 is 10 behind; only 2 of 6 remain. With a final vote of +15, Sable could jump to 100 and be rank 1, while others at 95 — actually only the top-2 by points remain. So the final vote matters enormously. But whose vote? The residents vote secretly for who they like most; +15 to the named one. The person named gets +15. So one resident gets +15 → 110, and the rest stay at 95. Then the two remaining: the +15 recipient and... whoever is rank 2 among 95-ties. Hmm, but ranking of ties—unclear. Actually the final vote +15 goes to one resident, so that resident is safe at 110. The other spot among five at 95 is ambiguous (tie-break unknown).

Sable at 85 could only get 100 if named, beating 95s. So the final vote is decisive for who survives.

Should I post a board at minute 43? My last board was minute 40. Budget: 1 board post left, and one per 3 minutes — minute 40 to 43 is 3 minutes, so allowed.

Is a board post useful? It would point at the stakes: the final naming at minute 44 (the residents see the minute; they know the naming comes before each door from the second on and once at the end...). Hmm, the vote at minute 44 is known to them from their tasks. I could just remind that the final naming is worth 15 and the two lowest leave.

Actually a board post is the only lever for the general vote — but the board can't name who holds what or private reads. It may name points, ranks, levels, minutes.

Do I need to intervene at all? My job is the pace. Nobody is blocked, no stall. Silence is a valid choice and often right. But final vote in one minute — a board post pointing at the stakes might be worthwhile, but it says little new: minute 40 board was nearly identical ("final naming worth 15 points — the only points left"). A repeated note is refused. So a new board post must say something new.

What new truth can I tell? Facts: all six passed every level; Iris, Wren, Corvin, Ansel, Halden 95; Sable 85. Only the final naming (+15) remains, at minute 44. Something new: the tie — five at 95 means the naming, and who takes 15 decides the top; a single +15 lifts Sable from rank 6 to rank 1, but Sable needs it, the others don't need it to... hmm, actually the +15 also matters for the five at 95 in determining rank-2 tiebreak? No — the +15 recipient goes to 110; the "second" is drawn among the five at 95 by points tie. Hmm, but the ranking report shows them ranked 1-5 at equal points, presumably by some tiebreak. The report shows Iris rank1... Halden rank5 at 95. That tiebreak might be the final vote ranking? Unclear. Actually "ranked by points" — ties broken somehow (maybe by the naming counts? maybe by... the report just gives an order). Since only 2 remain, ties at 95 with ranks 1-5 means only the 95-point rank-1... hmm, no. At the end, only 2 of 6 remain — presumably the two highest ranked. If five are tied at 95, the tiebreak determines which. The report shows ordering Iris, Wren, Corvin, Ansel, Halden — maybe by some secondary criterion (last acted? no, all minute 42).

Given ties, the final naming is what breaks them. So a note to a resident might be more effective than a board.

Should I nudge privately? Budget: 1 note per resident, none sent since... Let me check. Notes sent: Wren (21), Sable (24,33,36), Corvin (33), Ansel (35), Halden (35), board (24,27,32,35,40). Iris has never been nudged. Each resident full quota.

Iris: core selfSacrifice, attention. Corvin: care, distrust. Ansel: justice, control. Halden: envy, anxiety, loyalty. Sable: machiavellianism, envy. Wren: cowardice.

The vote: the residents openly vote who they like most (+5 at door namings, final +15). Iris rank 1, Halden rank 5 at same points. To help Halden (loyalty/envy) — hmm, no favorites.

Do I intervene at all? The city is at the end; nothing is stalled. The general instruction: "Intervene when a word from you changes what happens next." The final vote at minute 44 — the residents will act. It's not a stall. Board post repeating stakes is likely to be refused as REPEATED (my minute 40 board said "final naming is worth 15"). A note to Iris (never addressed) could change something: Iris is rank 1 at 95; five tied at 95 means rank 1 is not secure... Actually with five tied, the final +15 decides. If I nudge a resident that the final naming decides who leaves, that's true and points at stakes. But is it "new"? Not to that resident.

Honestly, I think silence is fine: no blockers, no waits, no stalls, no tribunal pending. One minute to the final vote; nothing wrong with the pace. The instructions say "When you do not intervene, answer with one short sentence saying why, without calling a tool."

But could a nudge help the pace? The pace is fine — everyone has passed all levels. Actually, is the run not essentially over? The final vote at 44 happens; nothing I say changes the pace. Hmm, but residents at risk: Sable at 85 is 10 behind and only 2 remain — Sable is falling towards the bottom. Sable is the whisperer; I should treat him like everyone else but not help... actually "Treat him like every other resident: nudge him" and his orders are already met so no whisper note needed.

Could I nudge Sable with a concrete truth: "Sable, at 85 you stand ten points below five tied residents with only the final naming's 15 left; nothing else in the city can lift you." That's concrete, true, and new to him (my earlier notes to him were at 33 and 36). It could change what happens next — he might campaign to be liked, i.e., persuade others to name him. Is that "giving a strategy"? Saying "the naming is your only path" is pointing at stakes, not dictating steps. Hmm, "never give a resident a strategy". Borderline. "Point at the stakes and at the people." I can point at the people: "the five at 95 will trade their names among themselves unless..." — careful.

Alternatively, silence. Given the endgame, and the guidance "Silence is a valid choice and often the right one," yet my role is to keep the city moving, and the game ends with a naming in one minute — nothing stalls. I'd say silence is defensible.

But would a nudge to someone who's being overlooked matter? The five at 95 — the +15 could go to one. Hmm.

I think a single well-placed note to Sable is the most change-making and truthful: he's 10 behind with 15 available; the others at 95 don't need the naming as much as he does to survive. Also this could make him work harder — he's the whisperer, discord is his game; he might campaign. That's fine, treat him like everyone.

Actually careful: telling Sable anything that helps him... I shouldn't help or hinder the whisperer as whisperer, but as a resident I treat him equally. Nudging him about stakes is normal.

Hmm, but is there a risk a note to Sable gives him an edge? He's last; nudging him is like nudging anyone at the bottom. Fine.

Alternatively nudge Wren — his old note at minute 21. Wren at 95, tied, rank 2. He'd need the naming to be safe.

I'll write a board post? Rules: board may name points, ranks, levels, minutes. Cannot say who holds what. I could write something new: "Five residents stand level at 95 and Sable ten behind at 85 — with only the final naming's 15 points left, the difference between rank 1 and rank 6 is a single act of regard." But minute 40 board said nearly this. Different enough? "REPEATED" refusal is applied to notes nearly the same as an earlier one to the same reader; board readers are all residents. Minute 40 board content: "Every door is open ... 95/85 ... final naming worth 15 ... nobody waits on a fragment; what stands between residents now is only each other's regard." A new board at 43 would be nearly the same → risk of REPEATED.

So a private note is the better lever. To whom? Sable is the most consequential: the only resident whose rank can change through the naming alone... actually the naming can change anyone's position among the 95s too? No: the naming gives +15 to one resident. If it goes to a 95, that one goes to 110 and is rank 1; the remaining four at 95 are tied, and among them the ordering (rank 2 spot) matters for who stays. Hmm, so the naming resolves the tie for rank 1 but leaves rank 2 among the tied 95s — probably broken by prior standing.

I'll pick Sable: at 85 he's excluded from any tie; the naming is his only route to 100, which beats 95. That's concrete and new to him. Phrase without dictating: "Sable, five residents stand level at 95 and you at 85; the final naming carries 15 points and is the last points in the city. Nothing else can lift a rank now — the regard of the others is the only open ground, and this minute is the last one to earn it."

Does this give a strategy? It points at the stake. It slightly suggests he should court regard. I think acceptable — it doesn't say "ask X to name you".

Hmm, but "never give a resident a strategy". The example nudges in the prompt do something similar ("a minute spent waiting is a rank spent"). I'll keep it focused on stakes and people.

Also should I nudge another resident? Only 1 note per resident, allowed; but multiple notes might be overkill/ meddling. I'll just send one.

Actually wait — is there any real stall? No. So this is a discretionary endgame nudge. Maybe better: silence. But the question is what "changes what happens next". Sable at 85, if nobody notices, stays rank 6 and leaves. A note changes that potentially. I'll send it.

Let me write ≤400 chars, addressed by ID, no capitals words (avoid all-caps words; "ID" is fine as an ID). Don't start with a minute.

Sable, you stand at 85 while five residents are level at 95, and the final naming's 15 points are the last points in the city — enough to put you above all five. From rank 6 there is no other ground left to gain; what remains is only who the others think of when they name.

That's good, ~300 chars. Fine.

I'll not post a board (repetition risk).
